newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Sonia Gandhi keeps the pundits guessing.
newsitem.headline: India's Sonia Gandhi keeps the pundits guessing.

text.p: As the sixth anniversary of former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi's assassination approaches, a whirl of speculation gathered about the political ambitions of his Italian-born widow Sonia, analysts said on Thursday.
While rumours spread about her future plans, the only event an aide would confirm was her attendance at a commemoration on May 21 in Delhi for her slain husband.

"She will definitely be visiting the memorial of her late husband at Veer Bhumi in Delhi May 21," he said, brushing off reports that she will hold a rally in the southern state of Tamil Nadu next Wednesday, where her husband was killed.
Since her husband's death in 1991, Sonia Gandhi, 50, had spurned repeated efforts to enter politics but last Thursday she officially became a member of the Congress party. She had enrolled in March.
Congress, dominated by the Gandhi-Nehru dynasty which has held sway over India for 38 of the 50 years since independence from Britian in 1947, is set to hold party presidency elections on June 9.
The Times of India on Thursday reported that Congress President Sitaram Kesri was looking at other options in case Sonia, as she is known throughout the country, wants the party throne.

Congress party officials saidKesri might seek election as India's figurehead leader in July, when President Shankar Dayal Sharma's term ends. Aspirants to the Congress party presidency must file their nominations by May 28.
"By then she (Sonia) has to make up her mind. We shall all be watching for that," commented Rasheed Talib, an independent political analyst.
One rival to Kesri, former minister A.R. Antulay, has said he will withdraw from the contest if Sonia takes over from the 77-year-old incumbent.
Sonia has yet to step into the full glare of India's political spotlight after paying the one rupee (two U.S. cent) fee to become an ordinary primary member of Congress.

Up until the surprise announcement of her membership last week, she had steadfastly stayed out of the country's mainstream political life since her husband was killed by a Tamil separatist's suicide bomb attack.

The question is what role she plans to take in the party, and the ramifications for Congress and the minority United Front government led by Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral, which depends on Congress support for survival.
"Mona Lisa makes her move", the weekly news magazine Outlook commented on its front cover under a picture of Sonia's face transposed onto the Leonardo Da Vinci masterpiece.
While Sonia has remained a political enigma engaged in discrete drawing room politics at her Delhi residence, she has in the past managed to stay aloof from the cut and thrust of party politics.
The most commonly cited reason for Sonia's emergence from the wings is Congress' desperation to invoke the magic of the Gandhi family name to revive its fortunes.
There are strong expectatiojs that India will have mid-term polls, at which the main opposition Hindu Nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) is best placed to make ground, analysts said.

The timing of her announced entry into the party came just days before the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) submitted a report to the government seeking approval to prosecute in a kickback scandal going back to Rajiv Gandhi's time as prime minister.

The Indian Express newspaper reported this week that the CBI named Rajiv Gandhi as a central figure in a web of intrigue in which middlemen and civil servants are alleged to have taken a cut in a $1.3 billion deal to buy artillery from Swedish armsmaker Bofors AB.
The Express said the CBI gave no evidence that Gandhi had benefited financially.
But, The Pioneer newspaper said on Thursday the CBI report showed the Prime Ministers' Office was implicated but Gandhi, himself, was not named.
